_method.authored: 2026-10-25. The blind queries were written and hashed before any crawl ran; the expectation-informed queries were written after reading the index's heading paths.
_method.rule: A query that misses STAYS in this file, unedited. Rewording a query until it passes overfits to a moving test set and destroys the measurement.
_method.blindness: blind:true queries were written from knowledge of each project's documentation, before the index existed. blind:false queries were written after reading the index's heading paths and are reported separately, so they cannot inflate the blind hit rate.
_method.expectation_corrections: Some blind expect values were changed after authoring, and each change is recorded in the query's note. Two kinds were allowed: correcting an expect to the intended page's live title, read from the site itself (its llms.txt or the page's h1) rather than from the index; and narrowing an expect that matched many pages to the intended page. Narrowing can only turn a hit into a miss. No query text was changed, and no expect was widened.
_method.dropped: One blind query was dropped before scoring: it asked how to migrate package.json scripts to moon, and the page that answered it no longer exists on the live site. Its id is reused by an informed query.
_method.expect_semantics: Every document is a crawled site with no section numbering, so 'expect' is a case-insensitive substring of heading_path. A site whose hierarchy came from URL paths renders each page's path segments as the first heading levels (for example 'Guides > Docker'), and some expects name that path rather than the page title.

categories.heading-term: an exact technical term that appears in a page title or heading
categories.body-term: a term, option or flag that appears only in body text
categories.conceptual-slang: how an agent or developer would phrase the need, in words the page does not use
categories.figure-dominated: the answer sits mostly in a code block, a table or a listing rather than in prose
categories.spans-boundary: the answer plainly continues across headings within a page

_method.sites: Crawled 2026-10-25 from docs.pytest.org/en/stable, www.sphinx-doc.org/en/master, moonrepo.dev/docs, rust-lang.github.io/mdBook and mintlify.com/docs. The sites change, so a re-crawl can move a baseline without any code change; compare builds against the same crawl date.
